messages.subject: Bug in gl.sexlinkage?
parts:
I have just started working with the dartr package to potentially identify sex linked markers, and believe I have come across a bug in the gl.sexlinkage function.

I have loaded my data (AMGL<- gl.read.dart(filename = "Report_DAmh19-4061_SNP_2.csv", ind.metafile = "AMDart_metadata.csv"), and explored the resulting genlight object, receiving the following output

 /// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 91 genotypes,  119,156 binary SNPs, size: 105.2 Mb
 2513252 (23.18 %) missing data

 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 91 SNPbin
   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)

 // Optional content
   @ind.names:  91 individual labels
   @loc.names:  119156 locus labels
   @loc.all:  119156 alleles
   @position: integer storing positions of the SNPs
   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 91-91)
   @other: a list containing: loc.metrics  ind.metrics 

When I try to run the gl.sexlinkage function (gl.sexlinkage(AMGL,t.het = 0, t.hom = 0, v =3) I am given the following error message

Error in `ploidy<-`(`*tmp*`, value = ploidy(x)[i]) : NA values provided

Ploidy was defined in my genlight object as having a range of 2-2 (see above), and checking ploidy(AMGL,"genlight") further confirmed that every single sample has a ploidy value of 2, without a single NA value. 

Any suggestions on how to deal with this issue would be greatly appreciated. 

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Bug in gl.sexlinkage?
parts:
OK, looking at your data it appears that the variable sex is recoded to M, F and NA when the input data has it as M, F and Unknown. I am not sure why this is happening, but recoding the sex==NA to sex <- "Unknown" fixes the problem I think. I will look into why this happens, and in particular, why the NA values are causing problems.

A

messages.author: 66537eeccf3193f3
messages.subject: Re: Bug in gl.sexlinkage?
parts:
Hi Sarah, 

I have just tried the script with my data too. I removed NA from the data and everything works fine. Here is the script.

#Check column name to make sure there is a sex column in ind.metrics
names(gl@other$ind.metrics)

#Subset samples with only F and M
pop(gl) <- gl@other$ind.metrics$sex
gl_s <- gl.keep.pop(gl,pop.list=c("F","M"))

#Filter potential sex-linked loci
gl.sexlinkage(gl_s)

Hope this helps.

R.
